sentences.text: Paralitherizinosaurus was an extinct therizinosaurid theropod dinosaur, a group of feathered carnivores that evolved into large, plant-eating forms.
The genus contains only one known species, P. japonicus, which is known from a partial right hand and a single neck bone.
Its name combines Greek words meaning 'tidal' and 'scythe' with the Latin word for 'lizard', while the species name refers to its discovery in Japan.
Paralitherizinosaurus is the youngest therizinosaur known to have lived in Japan.
It holds the distinction of being the first named therizinosaur from the country, even though two other unnamed specimens of the group exist.
Remains of this animal were first described by Murakami et al. in 2008 as an indeterminate maniraptoran theropod with possible therizinosauroid affinities.
The genus Paralitherizinosaurus was formally established by Kobayashi et al. in 2022.
Phylogenetic analyses place Paralitherizinosaurus in an unresolved clade with Therizinosaurus, Suzhousaurus, and an unnamed therizinosaurid from Uzbekistan.
Paralitherizinosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 83 and 75 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Paralitherizinosaurus is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
